title: Deep Research Agent
subtitle: Design a read-only research agent over the public web and a user's private documents that cites every claim, shows its gaps instead of faking certainty, and never lets the web side reach private data.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Oracle, eight numbers and discovery
practice_prompts.hint: Restate in one sentence, name the citation oracle, and ask about private scope, failed tools, completion and the $0.20 cap.

practice_prompts.label: State, trust zones and architecture
practice_prompts.hint: Trace the Acme question through the reducer, schema boundary, ledger, grader, verifier and egress firewall.

practice_prompts.label: Arithmetic and cost levers
practice_prompts.hint: Derive 28, 100, 120 and 170 aloud, then bring a naive seven-step run under $0.20.

practice_prompts.label: Bounds, gaps and the falsifying metric
practice_prompts.hint: Bound the loop four ways, walk the failure ladder with EMPTY vs UNAVAILABLE, and name the grade distribution.

rubric: Names the oracle (every claim cited to a source a reviewer would accept) and says read-only means no approval subsystem, on purpose.
Gives web sub-agents zero document scope and puts user identity in retrieval and cache keys, not only the prompt.
Merges evidence with an accumulating reducer and sums the budget across branches, explaining the last-write-wins loss.
Derives ~28/min, ~100/min peak, ~120 in flight and ~170 slots, and says Little's Law needs the mean, not p95.
Explains that the rendered answer is an exfiltration channel and puts an egress firewall on rendering as well as tools.
Bounds the loop with a done flag, hop cap, no-progress signature and per-run budget, each returning partial results with a reason.
Types EMPTY apart from UNAVAILABLE and degrades a failed branch to a named gap instead of silence or a guess.
Evaluates trajectory as well as outcome and names the grade distribution after correction as the falsifying metric.
Justifies multi-agent by parallelism, permissions or context, and answers the cost pivot with measure, route, bound, cache safely.

editorial_review.evidence: Re-review against all 46 captured sections. The previous version had 46 one-per-section rows with shared boilerplate evidence and had thinned or dropped: the Acme CEO trace (main-intro), the functional list, the non-functional target table and interview shortcut, the opening-move timing and 'is that the system?' quote, context rot and lost-in-the-middle, 'stop too early vs never stop', the outcome-vs-trajectory six-wasted-hops example, the what-to-test list, two of the supervisor build's four costs, the platform's four delta pieces, both two-minute answers, the eight carrying lines, the 60-second close, the four cost verbs, the references' supported claims, and 9 of 14 takeaways; it also reworded several check-yourself questions, rendered the 45-minute table's last cell as ', ', left the cost card with empty headers, and captioned every figure 'source figure N'. Rewrote into a 12-step walkthrough mirroring the full design's order, 9 deep dives (trust, evidence records, cost, grader, supervisor build, platform, three variants, references), 9 practice groups with 25 reveals, and 4 Quick review groups, giving 117 item-level rows. Defined terms before use (agent, sub-agent, ledger, reducer, last-write-wins, oracle, Little's Law, prefix caching, trifecta, exfiltration, control plane, trust zones, grade distribution), added worked examples (Acme trace, three-branch loss, $0.80 per-branch budget, image-URL exfiltration, 117→120 arithmetic, 10/15/20-second parallel latency), recast the source author's first-person 'my own build' as attributed, and labelled additions (reserve-then-reconcile budget, follow-up applications, two changed-constraint drills). Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): section 4 figure lead-ins one figure off → each figure introduced by what its SVG draws, meta note removed; 'after 12 hops' discovery question vs eight-hop cap and 3-12-step plan → question set to eight hops (the cap the termination code enforces), steps and hops stated as separate counters; 'roughly $0.20' vs '$0.20 ceiling' → ceiling throughout, because the budget dict, failure ladder and state table all enforce it as a per-run stop (whether the business treats it as hard stays a discovery question); 'this enterprise case' vs consumer product → consumer product that holds private documents, so it still needs per-user ACLs and a release gate. The summary paragraph listing these in the references section is removed.
